post.caption:
For most of spaceflight history every rocket was thrown away after one use, not out of waste but because landing one was thought impossible. A returning booster is empty, fast and too light to throttle down gently, so you relight briefly at exactly the right moment, steer with grid fins and unfold legs in the last seconds. It lands on a boat because that is where the trajectory already goes. Cost per kilogram to orbit fell roughly twentyfold in a decade, and everything else depends on that number.
